ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a thin insulating wire of length $L$ is fixed at the upper end and attached to a charged small ball of mass $m$ at the lower end. The entire setup is placed in a uniform electric field with a magnitude of $E$ and a direction horizontally to the right. It is known that when the wire deviates from the vertical direction by an angle $\theta$, the ball is in equilibrium. Given the gravitational acceleration $g$, determine:

1. What type of charge does the small ball carry?
2. What is the amount of electric charge?
3. If the small ball is pulled to the lowest point and released with no initial velocity, what is the magnitude of the velocity when the ball reaches the position shown in the diagram?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the upper end of the thin string is fixed on a ceiling-like support; a vertical dashed line is drawn downward from the fixed point, representing the vertical direction; the length of the thin string is labeled L, and it deviates to the right from the vertical direction, with the deviation angle labeled θ; the small ball is at the lower end of the thin string; multiple horizontal arrows in the figure all point to the right, with E labeled beside them, representing that the direction of the uniform electric field is horizontally to the right. Reasoning: At the inclined equilibrium position shown in the figure, the small ball is subjected to three forces: gravity mg vertically downward, the tension T of the thin string along the thin string pointing toward the suspension point, and the electric field force horizontal. The small ball deviates to the right relative to the vertical direction, and the electric field direction is also to the right, so for equilibrium, the electric field force should be to the right, so the small ball carries positive charge. Resolve the tension at equilibrium: in the vertical direction T cosθ = mg, and in the horizontal direction T sinθ = qE. Dividing the two equations gives tanθ = qE / mg, so q = mg tanθ / E. Since it has already been judged to carry positive charge, the amount of charge is the positive mg tanθ / E. Released from rest from the lowest point to the position shown in the figure, the thin string turns through angle θ. The height by which the small ball rises is L(1 - cosθ), and its displacement to the right is L sinθ. The work done by gravity W_g = -mgL(1 - cosθ), and the work done by the electric field force W_E = qEL sinθ. From the equilibrium relation qE = mg tanθ, obtain the net work W = mgL tanθ sinθ - mgL(1 - cosθ) = mgL(secθ - 1). By the kinetic energy theorem, 1/2 mv^2 = mgL(1/cosθ - 1), so v = sqrt(2gL(1/cosθ - 1)).

The entire setup is placed in a uniform electric field with a magnitude of $E$ and a direction horizontally to the right. It is known that when the wire deviates from the vertical direction by an angle $\theta$, the ball is in equilibrium. Given the gravitational acceleration $g$, determine:

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the pivot is at the ceiling, the dashed line is vertical downward, the string of length L is tilted to the right by angle theta, and the uniform electric-field arrows point horizontally to the right. Use force equilibrium at the shown tilted position: tension acts along the string toward the pivot, gravity mg is downward, and the electric force is horizontal. Since the ball is displaced to the right in a rightward field, the electric force must be rightward, so the charge is positive. Resolve forces: T cos theta = mg and T sin theta = qE, giving q = mg tan theta / E. For the speed from the lowest point to the shown position, use work-energy. From the lowest point to angle theta, the ball rises by L(1 - cos theta), and moves right by L sin theta. Gravity does work -mgL(1 - cos theta); the electric field does work qEL sin theta. Insert qE = mg tan theta, so net work = mgL[tan theta sin theta - (1 - cos theta)] = mgL(sec theta - 1). Then 1/2 mv^2 equals this net work, giving v = sqrt(2gL(1/cos theta - 1)).

平衡时分解拉力：竖直方向 T cosθ = mg，水平方向 T sinθ = qE。两式相除得 tanθ = qE / mg，所以 q = mg tanθ / E。因为已判断带正电，所以电荷量为正的 mg tanθ / E。

从最低点由静止释放到图示位置，细线转过角 θ。小球升高高度为 L(1 - cosθ)，向右位移为 L sinθ。重力做功 W_g = -mgL(1 - cosθ)，电场力做功 W_E = qEL sinθ。由平衡关系 qE = mg tanθ，得净功 W = mgL tanθ sinθ - mgL(1 - cosθ) = mgL(secθ - 1)。由动能定理，1/2 mv^2 = mgL(1/cosθ - 1)，所以 v = sqrt(2gL(1/cosθ - 1))。

2. 电荷量：q = mg tanθ / E。
3. 到达图示位置时速度大小：v = sqrt(2gL(1/cosθ - 1))。

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the field lines labeled E point right, the ball hangs at an angular coordinate theta to the right of the vertical, and the wire length is L. Treat the combined gravity-plus-electric force as producing an effective constant-force potential along the pendulum arc. At an arbitrary angle phi from the downward vertical toward the right, the tangential force is qE cos phi - mg sin phi. The shown position is an equilibrium, so at phi = theta, qE cos theta = mg sin theta. This implies qE = mg tan theta; because qE is rightward while E is rightward, q is positive, and q = mg tan theta / E. For the speed, integrate the tangential work along the circular arc from phi = 0 to phi = theta: W = integral_0^theta L(qE cos phi - mg sin phi)dphi = L(qE sin theta - mg(1 - cos theta)). Reasoning: At the inclined equilibrium position shown in the figure, the small ball is subjected to three forces: gravity mg vertically downward, the tension T of the thin string along the thin string pointing toward the suspension point, and the electric field force horizontal. The small ball deviates to the right relative to the vertical direction, and the electric field direction is also to the right, so for equilibrium, the electric field force should be to the right, so the small ball carries positive charge.

Resolve the tension at equilibrium: in the vertical direction T cosθ = mg, and in the horizontal direction T sinθ = qE. Dividing the two equations gives tanθ = qE / mg, so q = mg tanθ / E. Since it has already been judged to carry positive charge, the amount of charge is the positive mg tanθ / E.

Released from rest from the lowest point to the position shown in the figure, the thin string turns through angle θ. The height by which the small ball rises is L(1 - cosθ), and its displacement to the right is L sinθ. The work done by gravity W_g = -mgL(1 - cosθ), and the work done by the electric field force W_E = qEL sinθ. From the equilibrium relation qE = mg tanθ, obtain the net work W = mgL tanθ sinθ - mgL(1 - cosθ) = mgL(secθ - 1). By the kinetic energy theorem, 1/2 mv^2 = mgL(1/cosθ - 1), so v = sqrt(2gL(1/cosθ - 1)).
